title: Single Worm Lysis Protocol
author: Ida Barlow
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.587g9zn

steps.title: Prepare 10X PCR Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the 10X PCR buffer (pH 8.3) and adjust pH using hydrochloric acid.

substeps.instruction: Combine 18.64 g KCl, 3.70 g Trizma base, 0.71 g Tris-HCl, and 3.70 g MgCl2 in 500 mL water.
Cool the solution (as temperature affects pH).
Use a pH meter and add hydrochloric acid to achieve pH 8.3.

steps.title: Prepare 1X PCR Buffer with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL of 1X PCR buffer containing 0.4 mg/ml Proteinase K (volumes can be scaled as required).

substeps.instruction: Combine 855 µL water, 50 µL 10X PCR buffer (pH 8.3), and 1000 µL of 20 mg/ml Proteinase K solution.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare 200 µL PCR tubes with the lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Allow 15 µL of 1X PCR buffer + PK per worm.
Pipette buffer into the lid of the PCR tube (up to 45 µL can fit into the tube lid).

steps.title: Pick Worms
steps.instruction: Transfer individual worms into the lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Pick a single worm at a time into the liquid in the 200 µL PCR tube.
Verify that the worm is swimming in the buffer.

steps.title: Pellet Worms
steps.instruction: Secure the tubes and centrifuge to collect the sample.

substeps.instruction: Close the lids of the 200 µL tubes.
Spin in a microfuge so that the liquid and worms are at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Freeze Lysis
steps.instruction: Burst the cells open by freezing the tubes in a -80 °C freezer for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Incubate in Thermocycler
steps.instruction: Transfer tubes to a thermocycler and run the worm lysis program.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 60 °C for 1 hour and 10 minutes.

steps.title: Store and Use gDNA
steps.instruction: Store the extracted gDNA and use for subsequent PCR.

substeps.instruction: Store gDNA in a -20 °C freezer until required.
Use 2 µL of gDNA per 25 µL PCR reaction.
